lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say checks understanding of word meaning and pronunciation of activity phrases. Practise allows students to listen and repeat the phrases in a structured question and answer.
Look for careful listening, clear pronunciation and repetition of the target phrases, accurate sound-image recognition, and confident pronunciation.

“I asked my friends about their weekend plans, they told me lots of things but I can’t remember everything. I need to practise listening! Let’s listen to what the children said… that will help! Can you tell me what they said?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives controlled speaking practise with ‘He/She said that he/she was going to…’ structure, as students respond to picture cues with complete, accurate statements.
Look for clear questions and answers, accurate references to the pictures, and both partners taking turns to ask and answer.
“Look! Two friends are remembering what different people told them about their plans. Can you help them find out? You can use the pictures to help you.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.75 - A Solve and write the letters

details: Solve and write the letters reviews and reinforces the target weekend activity phrases using a simple code puzzle.
Look for correctly spelled phrases accurately matched to their corresponding pictures, neat handwriting, sounding out words as they write.
“It’s puzzle time! You know I love puzzles. Let’s be detectives! Each number stands for a letter. How about we crack the codes together to find out about different weekend activities.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.75 - B Look and tick

details: Look and tick checks understanding of reported-speech sentences by having students match ‘He/She said that…’ statements to the picture that shows each plan.
Look for correct ticks beside each sentence, students scanning the picture for clues, and the ability to read a sentence aloud and point to the matching person and activity.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - Speaking Board Game

details: Board game provides freer speaking practice with the reported-speech pattern as students move across the board, identify activities from pictures, and produce personalised ‘He/She said that…’ sentences.
Look for active participation in the game, students using “What did he/she say?” and “He/She said that…” without much prompting, accurate use of activity phrases, and natural turn-taking.

“Let’s play a game to find out what the children did on the weekend. There are lots of cool activities. I want to do them too! Are you ready? Who is going to be the winner? Do you think you can beat me?! Let’s go!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (closed pairs): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (open pairs): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
